title: The Sculpture That Keeps a Secret

pages.text: Mr Asiedu showed the class a photograph of a tall, curved sheet of copper covered in cut-out letters. “This sculpture is called Kryptos,” he said. “It stands in the grounds of the CIA headquarters in Virginia, in the United States. The letters look like nonsense. Almost all of them are a secret message.”
sentences: Mr Asiedu showed the class a photograph of a tall, curved sheet of copper covered in cut-out letters.
“This sculpture is called Kryptos,” he said.
“It stands in the grounds of the CIA headquarters in Virginia, in the United States.
The letters look like nonsense.
Almost all of them are a secret message.”
pages.alt: A teacher shows a photograph of a curved copper sculpture covered in letters.

pages.text: “An artist named Jim Sanborn made it, and it was dedicated in 1990,” said Mr Asiedu. “He worked with a retired code expert called Edward Scheidt. The sculpture carries four coded messages, totalling 869 characters. Scientists call the four parts K1, K2, K3 and K4.” Kelvin did the sum on his calculator. “K4 has 97 letters. That is about 11 percent.”

pages.text: “K1, K2 and K3 have been solved,” said Mr Asiedu. “A team at the National Security Agency in the early 1990s solved them, but that was kept secret for years. A CIA analyst solved them in 1998. And in 1999, a computer scientist named Jim Gillogly announced the first public solutions.” Hajara wrote: three solved, three different teams.

pages.alt: A timeline shows three solutions by different people over several years.

pages.text: “And K4?” asked Hajara. “K4 stayed unsolved for more than thirty years,” said Mr Asiedu. “Hundreds of thousands of people tried. It starts with the letters O-B-K-R and has only 97 letters. That is not much to work with. That is why some codes are harder: less text gives fewer patterns to spot.”

pages.alt: A row of 97 letters on a board, with the first four circled.

pages.text: “Over the years, the artist released clues,” said Mr Asiedu. “Certain letters in K4 stand for the word BERLIN. Others stand for CLOCK, then NORTHEAST, then EAST. Each clue was a small window into the plaintext, the hidden message. But even with the clues, nobody could prove a full solution.”

pages.alt: Four clue words appear on cards: BERLIN, CLOCK, NORTHEAST, EAST.

pages.text: “Then, in 2025, things changed,” said Mr Asiedu. “The artist announced he would auction his K4 solution. Two journalists, Jarett Kobek and Richard Byrne, looked through his papers in a public archive at the Smithsonian. They said they found scraps that revealed the hidden text, and they sent it to the artist, who confirmed it was accurate.”

pages.alt: Two people look through boxes in an archive while a letter is passed to an artist.

pages.text: “The K4 solution was sold at auction for $962,500 to a buyer who has not been named,” said Mr Asiedu. “The journalists promised not to publish the text. So the public still cannot read K4, and some cryptographers say we still need to see the method, not only the answer. And there may be a fifth message to come.”

pages.text: Kelvin thought for a moment. “So it is solved and not solved at the same time,” he said. “Solved by the artist, and perhaps by two journalists. Unsolved for everyone else.” “And proven?” asked Mr Asiedu. “Not independently,” said Hajara. “A good answer needs a method anyone can check.” “That,” said Mr Asiedu, “is the heart of cryptography.” The end.

activities.question: How many of Kryptos’s four coded sections were solved by the 1990s?

activities.prompt: The artist released clue words from K4. How could clues help a codebreaker?
options: They show part of the hidden message, so the method can be tested

activities.question: Why do some experts say the answer alone is not enough?
options: They want to see the method so anyone can check it
They think the text is too long

activities.definition: The ordinary, readable message before it is turned into a code.

activities.prompt: Put the Kryptos story in order.
items: K1 to K3 were solved by different people.
The artist released clues about K4.
K4’s hidden text was sold at auction in 2025.

activities.prompt: People worked on K4 for decades without success. What keeps you going when a problem is very hard?

glossary.definition: The readable message before it is turned into a code.
The study of making and breaking secret codes.
A sale where people bid, and the highest bidder buys the item.
A place that keeps important documents and records.
